title: SWE-DIVE: Multi-Turn Coding Agent Evaluation with Dynamic User Simulation
title_zh: SWE-DIVE：基于动态用户模拟的多轮编码智能体评估

paragraphs.en: Grounded User Simulation for Model Evaluation and Training: Diversity, Fidelity, and Validity
paragraphs.zh: 面向模型评估与训练的接地用户模拟：多样性、保真度与有效性

paragraphs.en: Coding agents are typically evaluated using one-shot, well-formulated prompts. Benchmarks such as SWE-bench use existing GitHub issues as input for a coding agent and evaluate whether the agent successfully solves the task. However, in real-world use cases, prompts are often not as well-formulated or structured as existing GitHub issues. Additionally, a coding agent session is not limited to a single prompt; it typically involves a multi-turn interaction in which the user iteratively adds new tasks and requirements that the agent must fulfill.
paragraphs.zh: 编程智能体通常使用一次性的、表述完善的提示词进行评估。 像 SWE-bench 这样的基准测试使用现有的 GitHub 议题作为编程智能体的输入，并评估该智能体是否成功完成任务。 然而，在实际使用场景中，提示词往往不像现有的 GitHub 议题那样表述完善或结构清晰。 此外，编程智能体的会话并不局限于单个提示词；它通常涉及多轮交互，用户在交互中不断提出新的任务和要求，智能体必须予以完成。

paragraphs.en: To benchmark these abilities, we developed SWE-DIVE, a dynamic, interactive validation and evaluation framework for benchmarking coding agents in a multi-turn environment. To achieve this, we introduce a user simulator that can simulate different behavioral patterns and communicate with the coding agent. We also introduce a conversation validator that evaluates the user simulator’s outputs to determine whether they fulfill the initial requirements and guide the agent toward successfully solving the task. The entire framework is embedded in a Harbor environment, which orchestrates the coding agent, user simulator, and conversation validator, and executes the test environment to determine whether the agent successfully solves the task. Our results and source code are available in our GitHub repository ( https://github.com/lorenzbrehme/swe-dive_usersim ).
paragraphs.zh: 为了对这些能力进行基准测试，我们开发了 SWE-DIVE，这是一个动态的交互式验证与评估框架，用于在多轮环境中对编码智能体进行基准测试。 为实现这一目标，我们引入了一个用户模拟器，它可以模拟不同的行为模式并与编码智能体进行通信。 我们还引入了一个对话验证器，用于评估用户模拟器的输出，判断其是否满足初始需求，并引导智能体成功解决任务。 整个框架嵌入在 Harbor 环境中，该环境负责协调编码智能体、用户模拟器和对话验证器，并执行测试环境以确定智能体是否成功解决任务。 我们的结果和源代码可在我们的 GitHub 仓库中获取（ https://github.com/lorenzbrehme/swe-dive_usersim ）。

paragraphs.en: Agents are typically evaluated on benchmarks collected from GitHub issues or crafted for a certain task, like SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al.,, 2024 ) . However, the input format of a complete, detailed github issue is not how users normally interact with agents – users often give a high-level prompt that is lacking detail and iterate on the prototype until it’s complete ( Baumann et al.,, 2026 ) . In other words, agent prompting is a process of iteratively defining the problem rather than a one-shot attempt.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体通常在从 GitHub issue 收集或为特定任务构建的基准上进行评估，例如 SWE-bench（Jimenez et al.,, 2024）。 然而，完整且详细的 GitHub issue 这种输入格式并不是用户通常与智能体交互的方式——用户往往给出一个缺乏细节的高层次提示，并对原型进行迭代直至其完成（Baumann et al.,, 2026）。 换句话说，智能体提示是一个迭代式定义问题的过程，而非一次性的尝试。

paragraphs.en: Baumann et al., (2026) investigated the behavior of humans using a coding agent and found that the agent is used in multi-turn interactions, where different roles emerge, such as the expert nitpicker or the ambiguous programmer. These multi-turn behaviors are already studied in benchmarks such as CodeFlowBench ( Wang et al.,, 2026 ) and CodeGen ( Nijkamp et al.,, 2023 ) , which evaluate coding agents in multi-turn settings. In these benchmarks, tasks typically involve iteratively adding new features, requiring the agent to continually adapt and find solutions. Additionally, AmbigSWE-bench explores the ambiguous behavior of users by providing ambiguous instructions and allowing the agent to ask clarification questions in order to resolve this ambiguity ( Vijayvargiya et al.,, 2025 ) . These multi-turn benchmarks follow a predefined process and do not adapt depending on what the agents ask. Baumann et al., (2026) demonstrates that 41% of the turns were pushbacks, indicating that the agent did not perform as the user expected and that clarification was needed. In addition, Vijayvargiya et al., (2025) shows that the agent is still prompted with the full task list, whereas a more realistic setup involves users providing very nitpicky and vague instructions, iteratively adding new tasks in a multi-turn conversation.
paragraphs.zh: Baumann 等人（2026）研究了人类使用编码智能体的行为，发现智能体是在多轮交互中被使用的，其中会出现不同的角色，例如“挑剔专家”或“模糊程序员”。 这些多轮行为已经在 CodeFlowBench（Wang 等人，2026）和 CodeGen（Nijkamp 等人，2023）等基准中被研究，这些基准在多轮设置下评估编码智能体。 在这些基准中，任务通常涉及迭代式地添加新功能，要求智能体不断适应并寻找解决方案。 此外，AmbigSWE-bench 通过提供模糊的指令并允许智能体提出澄清问题以消除这种模糊性，来探索用户的模糊行为（Vijayvargiya 等人，2025）。 这些多轮基准遵循预定义的流程，不会根据智能体所提出的问题进行调整。 Baumann 等人（2026）表明，41% 的轮次是“反驳”，这表明智能体的表现不符合用户的预期，需要进一步澄清。 此外，Vijayvargiya 等人（2025）表明，智能体仍然会被给予完整的任务列表，而更现实的场景是用户提供非常挑剔和模糊的指令，并在多轮对话中迭代式地添加新任务。

paragraphs.en: To overcome these challenges, we introduce a dynamic interactive validation and evaluation benchmark, SWE-DIVE, that builds upon the DIVE methodology, originally proposed for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation systems ( Brehme et al.,, 2026 ) . SWE-DIVE transforms existing software engineering benchmarks, such as SWE-bench, into dynamic, interactive evaluation environments. It splits the original tasks into incremental sub-tasks and uses an LLM to simulate the user’s discovery process.
paragraphs.zh: 为克服这些挑战，我们提出一个动态交互式验证与评估基准 SWE-DIVE，它基于最初为评估检索增强生成系统而提出的 DIVE 方法论（Brehme et al.,, 2026）。 SWE-DIVE 将现有的软件工程基准（如 SWE-bench）转化为动态、交互式的评估环境。 它将原始任务拆分为增量式的子任务，并使用大语言模型来模拟用户的探索过程。

sents.en: It splits the original tasks into incremental sub-tasks and uses an LLM to simulate the user’s discovery process.
sents.zh: 它将原始任务拆分为增量式的子任务，并使用大语言模型来模拟用户的探索过程。

paragraphs.en: Benchmarking software engineering agents requires a collection of tasks consisting of an existing codebase and a corresponding test suite that the agent must satisfy. Benchmarks such as SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al.,, 2024 ) and Terminal-Bench ( Merrill et al.,, 2026 ) provide such tasks by using existing software repositories containing issues that have already been resolved by human developers. Each task includes a predefined initial state, where the provided tests fail, and an expected final state, where the tests pass after the required code modifications have been applied.
paragraphs.zh: 对软件工程智能体进行基准测试需要一个任务集合，每个任务由一个现有代码库和一个智能体必须满足的对应测试套件组成。 SWE-bench（Jimenez et al.,, 2024）和 Terminal-Bench（Merrill et al.,, 2026）等基准测试通过使用现有的软件仓库来提供此类任务，这些仓库中包含已由人类开发者解决的问题。 每个任务都包含一个预定义的初始状态（此时提供的测试失败）和一个预期的最终状态（即在应用所需的代码修改后测试通过）。

sents.en: Benchmarking software engineering agents requires a collection of tasks consisting of an existing codebase and a corresponding test suite that the agent must satisfy.
sents.zh: 对软件工程智能体进行基准测试需要一个任务集合，每个任务由一个现有代码库和一个智能体必须满足的对应测试套件组成。

sents.en: Benchmarks such as SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al.,, 2024 ) and Terminal-Bench ( Merrill et al.,, 2026 ) provide such tasks by using existing software repositories containing issues that have already been resolved by human developers.

paragraphs.en: These tasks are typically provided to the agent through a single-shot prompt describing the issue to solve. After the agent modifies the codebase, the benchmark executes the associated test suite to determine whether the task has been successfully completed. The resulting success rate is then used as a metric to compare the performance of different software engineering agents.
paragraphs.zh: 这些任务通常通过单次提示（single-shot prompt）提供给智能体，提示中描述了需要解决的问题。 在智能体修改代码库之后，基准测试会执行相应的测试套件，以判断任务是否已成功完成。 由此得出的成功率随后被用作衡量指标，用于比较不同软件工程智能体的性能。

sents.en: These tasks are typically provided to the agent through a single-shot prompt describing the issue to solve.
sents.zh: 这些任务通常通过单次提示（single-shot prompt）提供给智能体，提示中描述了需要解决的问题。

sents.en: After the agent modifies the codebase, the benchmark executes the associated test suite to determine whether the task has been successfully completed.
sents.zh: 在智能体修改代码库之后，基准测试会执行相应的测试套件，以判断任务是否已成功完成。

paragraphs.en: To extend these benchmarks, approaches such as CodeFlowBench ( Wang et al.,, 2026 ) and CodeGen ( Nijkamp et al.,, 2023 ) introduce multi-turn interactions into the evaluation process. These benchmarks define a sequence of tasks that are provided iteratively to the agent, allowing it to complete multiple development steps over several interactions. Some approaches initialize agents from scratch ( Nijkamp et al.,, 2023 ; Orlanski et al.,, 2025 ) , while others build upon existing repositories by selecting and filtering issues or introducing additional requirements over multiple iterations, such as in CodeFlowBench ( Wang et al.,, 2026 ) . However, these benchmarks remain largely static, as the sequence of tasks and requirements is predefined. They do not capture realistic user behavior, where requirements evolve dynamically, users provide feedback, and goals may change during the development process ( Baumann et al.,, 2026 ; Vijayvargiya et al.,, 2025 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 为了扩展这些基准测试，CodeFlowBench（Wang et al., 2026）和 CodeGen（Nijkamp et al., 2023）等方法在评估过程中引入了多轮交互。 这些基准测试定义了一系列任务，并以迭代方式提供给智能体，使其能够在多次交互中完成多个开发步骤。 一些方法从零开始初始化智能体（Nijkamp et al., 2023；Orlanski et al., 2025），另一些方法则基于现有代码库，通过筛选和过滤问题（issue）或在多次迭代中引入额外需求来构建，例如 CodeFlowBench（Wang et al., 2026）。 然而，这些基准测试在很大程度上仍然是静态的，因为任务和需求的序列是预先定义好的。 它们无法刻画真实的用户行为，即在开发过程中需求动态演变、用户提供反馈、目标可能发生变化（Baumann et al., 2026；Vijayvargiya et al., 2025）。

paragraphs.en: Another approach for introducing multi-turn behavior is to provide feedback based on the final outcome of the agent’s implementation. In this setting, the agent receives information about whether the tests have passed and, if not, is provided with the test results to iteratively improve its solution ( Yang et al.,, 2023 ) . However, these benchmarks still rely on highly structured and formalized task descriptions.
paragraphs.zh: 引入多轮行为的另一种方法是基于智能体实现的最终结果提供反馈。 在这种设置中，智能体会接收关于测试是否通过的信息，如果未通过，则会获得测试结果，以便迭代地改进其解决方案（Yang et al.,, 2023）。 然而，这些基准测试仍然依赖于高度结构化和形式化的任务描述。

sents.en: Another approach for introducing multi-turn behavior is to provide feedback based on the final outcome of the agent’s implementation.
sents.zh: 引入多轮行为的另一种方法是基于智能体实现的最终结果提供反馈。

paragraphs.en: To address this limitation, Garg et al., (2025) modifies SWE-bench task descriptions to create more realistic user requests. Similar approaches introduce ambiguity into the task descriptions by incorporating different user personas, where the agent can ask clarification questions to obtain additional information before starting the implementation ( Vijayvargiya et al.,, 2025 ; Zhou et al.,, 2026 ) .

sents.en: Similar approaches introduce ambiguity into the task descriptions by incorporating different user personas, where the agent can ask clarification questions to obtain additional information before starting the implementation ( Vijayvargiya et al.,, 2025 ; Zhou et al.,, 2026 ) .
sents.zh: 类似的方法通过引入不同的用户画像在任务描述中加入模糊性，智能体可以在开始实现之前提出澄清问题以获取更多信息（ Vijayvargiya et al.,, 2025 ; Zhou et al.,, 2026 ） 。

paragraphs.en: Despite these improvements, an important aspect of realistic software development remains unexplored: users do not only clarify existing requirements but also introduce new tasks and requirements throughout the development process. Existing benchmarks primarily focus on solving a single predefined issue, whereas real-world interactions with coding agents often involve iterative collaboration, where users continuously refine goals and add new requests ( Baumann et al.,, 2026 ) . To address this gap, we introduce SWE-DIVE, a new benchmark-agnostic approach for evaluating coding agents through dynamic, multi-turn interactions that better reflect realistic user-agent collaboration.

paragraphs.en: SWE-DIVE is a dynamic, interactive validation and evaluation framework for benchmarking software engineering agents. It builds upon existing benchmarks, such as SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al.,, 2024 ) and Terminal-Bench ( Merrill et al.,, 2026 ) , by transforming single-turn benchmark tasks into multi-turn interactive evaluations. This is achieved through a user simulator that collaborates with the agent to complete the original benchmark tasks. The framework consists of three main components: the user simulator, the conversation validator, and the Task Completion Evaluator. The user simulator interacts with the evaluated agent, the conversation validator assesses the quality and validity of the interaction, and the Task Completion Evaluator determines whether the benchmark task has been completed successfully.
paragraphs.zh: SWE-DIVE 是一个动态、交互式的验证与评估框架，用于对软件工程智能体进行基准测试。 它在现有基准（例如 SWE-bench（Jimenez et al., 2024）和 Terminal-Bench（Merrill et al., 2026））的基础上，将单轮基准任务转化为多轮交互式评估。 这是通过一个与智能体协作以完成原始基准任务的用户模拟器来实现的。 该框架由三个主要组件构成：用户模拟器、对话验证器和任务完成评估器。 用户模拟器与被评估的智能体进行交互，对话验证器评估交互的质量与有效性，任务完成评估器则判断基准任务是否已被成功完成。

paragraphs.en: The first component of SWE-DIVE is the user simulator. This component leverages an LLM to simulate a user interacting with the evaluated software engineering agent. To achieve realistic user interactions, we ground the user simulator in existing, validated task descriptions that specify the underlying requirements and implementation context. This grounding enables the simulator to model a collaborative user who interactively discovers, clarifies, and refines requirements throughout the software implementation process. This distinguishes SWE-DIVE from existing benchmarks ( Wang et al.,, 2026 ; Nijkamp et al.,, 2023 ) , where interaction is primarily used to provide missing information rather than to model the iterative process of requirement discovery and refinement. The simulator presents the agent with tasks, responds to its questions, provides additional information as needed, and offers feedback based on the agent’s responses and modifications to the codebase. It iteratively advances the conversation by introducing follow-up requests or clarifications until the task has been completed successfully or no further progress can be made.
paragraphs.zh: SWE-DIVE 的第一个组件是用户模拟器。 该组件利用大语言模型来模拟与被评测软件工程智能体交互的用户。 为了实现真实的用户交互，我们将用户模拟器建立在现有的、经过验证的任务描述之上，这些描述明确了底层需求与实现背景。 这种依据使模拟器能够刻画一个协作型用户，在整个软件实现过程中以交互方式发现、澄清并完善需求。 这将 SWE-DIVE 与现有基准（Wang et al.,, 2026；Nijkamp et al.,, 2023）区分开来，在那些基准中，交互主要用于提供缺失的信息，而不是刻画需求发现与完善的迭代过程。 模拟器向智能体提出任务，回答其提问，按需提供额外信息，并根据智能体的回复及其对代码库的修改给出反馈。 模拟器通过提出后续请求或澄清来迭代推进对话，直到任务成功完成或无法取得进一步进展为止。

paragraphs.en: Before the interaction begins, the user simulator is assigned a role. We ground our user simulation in behavioral patterns from SWE-Chat ( Baumann et al.,, 2026 ) , which were derived from observations of real user interactions with coding agents. Specifically, we leverage three roles. The Expert Nitpicker maintains a stable overall goal while providing a series of precise, targeted corrections to the implementation. Each interaction refines how the agent implements the solution rather than what it is expected to build. The Vague Requester provides broad, underspecified instructions and delegates most implementation decisions to the agent. Finally, the Mind Changer reverses the overall goal during the interaction, fundamentally changing what the agent is expected to build rather than merely modifying the implementation details. These roles are not intended to represent distinct user populations or individual users. Rather, they capture diverse behavioral patterns observed in SWE-Chat and provide controlled conditions for studying how coding agents respond to different user behaviors.
paragraphs.zh: 在交互开始之前，用户模拟器会被分配一个角色。 我们将用户模拟建立在 SWE-Chat（Baumann 等人，2026）的行为模式之上，这些模式源自对真实用户与编码智能体交互的观察。 具体来说，我们采用了三种角色。 挑剔专家在保持总体目标稳定的同时，对实现提供一系列精确、有针对性的修正。 每次交互都会改进智能体实现解决方案的方式，而不是改变预期构建的内容。 模糊请求者提供宽泛、欠明确的指令，并将大多数实现决策委托给智能体。 最后，改主意者在交互过程中推翻总体目标，从根本上改变智能体预期构建的内容，而不仅仅是修改实现细节。 这些角色并不旨在代表不同的用户群体或个体用户。 相反，它们捕捉了在 SWE-Chat 中观察到的多样行为模式，并为研究编码智能体如何响应不同用户行为提供了受控条件。

paragraphs.en: In the first turn, the user simulator is prompted with the initial benchmark task . The complete task specification, such as the issue description from SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al.,, 2024 ) , is provided together with the reference solution describing the expected outcome. This original objective serves as the grounding for the user simulator, which provides the context needed to guide the interaction. Rather than following a predefined sequence of subtasks, the simulator adaptively determines what information, clarification, or requirement should be communicated next based on the agent’s progress. In each turn, the user simulator receives the agent’s latest response together with the changes made to the codebase and uses this information to validate and adjust its next message. This enables the simulator to adapt the interaction to the agent’s behavior while maintaining alignment with the original task objective.
paragraphs.zh: 在第一轮中，用户模拟器会收到初始基准任务作为提示。 完整的任务规范（例如来自 SWE-bench 的问题描述（Jimenez et al., 2024））与描述预期结果的参考解决方案一并提供。 这一原始目标为用户模拟器提供了依据，为引导交互提供所需的上下文。 用户模拟器并不遵循预定义的子任务序列，而是根据智能体的进展自适应地决定下一步应传达什么信息、澄清或需求。 在每一轮中，用户模拟器会接收智能体的最新回复以及代码库中的变更，并利用这些信息来验证和调整其下一条消息。 这使模拟器能够根据智能体的行为调整交互，同时保持与原始任务目标的一致性。

paragraphs.en: Once the user simulator determines that the overall task has been completed successfully, it returns ‘done’ instead of generating another prompt, thereby terminating the simulation. sents.zh: 在初始轮次和后续轮次中，对话验证器会对生成的用户提示进行评估。

sents.en: Each prompt must remain aligned with the original benchmark issue, follow the defined subtask trajectory, match the assigned user role, and be understandable and actionable for the agent.
sents.zh: 每个提示必须与原始基准问题保持一致，遵循既定的子任务轨迹，匹配所分配的用户角色，并对智能体而言易于理解和可执行。

paragraphs.en: For each validation step, the conversation validator returns a boolean value indicating whether the generated output is valid . If an output is considered invalid, the validator additionally provides a reason explaining why the output does not satisfy the requirements and how it can be improved. This feedback is used within the validation loop to prompt the user simulator again, allowing it to regenerate an improved output . This process continues until the validator approves the generated prompt. Once validated, the prompt is sent to the agent, which executes the requested task and provides its response back to the user simulator for the next interaction cycle .
paragraphs.zh: 对于每个验证步骤，对话验证器会返回一个布尔值，用于指示生成的输出是否有效。 如果某个输出被判定为无效，验证器还会提供原因，解释该输出为何不满足要求以及如何改进。 该反馈会在验证循环中用于再次提示用户模拟器，使其能够重新生成一个改进后的输出。 这一过程持续进行，直到验证器批准生成的提示。 验证通过后，该提示会被发送给智能体，智能体执行所请求的任务，并将其响应返回给用户模拟器，以进行下一轮交互循环。

paragraphs.en: The Task Completion Evaluator assesses the performance of the software engineering agent and provides quantitative metrics to enable a comprehensive evaluation. It is executed when either the maximum number of turns is reached or the user simulator determines that the conversation is complete. The Task Completion Evaluator leverages the execution environment of the original benchmark to verify whether the assigned task has been successfully completed and calculates the overall success rate. Upon completion of an evaluation, SWE-DIVE provides a comprehensive performance summary, including the average number of conversation turns, and a detailed analysis of the interactions. Furthermore, the evaluation metrics can be analyzed based on the assigned user role, allowing for a comparison of agent performance under different interaction scenarios. SWE-DIVE also enables filtering based on the number of required turns, providing insights into the efficiency and behavior of agents in realistic, multi-turn software engineering tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 任务完成评估器评估软件工程智能体的表现，并提供量化指标，以实现全面评估。 它在达到最大对话轮数或用户模拟器判定对话已结束时执行。 任务完成评估器利用原始基准的执行环境来验证所分配的任务是否已成功完成，并计算总体成功率。 评估完成后，SWE-DIVE 会提供全面的性能总结，包括平均对话轮数，以及对交互过程的详细分析。 此外，评估指标还可以根据所分配的用户角色进行分析，从而比较智能体在不同交互场景下的表现。 SWE-DIVE 还支持按所需轮数进行筛选，从而为智能体在真实的多轮软件工程任务中的效率和行为提供洞察。

paragraphs.en: Our experiments will use SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench tasks, both of which are supported by the Harbor framework. Currently, the main limitation is that we use the Git diff as input for the user simulator so that it can assess the agent’s progress. This information needs to be available for a benchmark to be directly usable with our framework; otherwise, the Git diff-based approach would need to be replaced with an alternative progress signal provided by the benchmark.

paragraphs.en: Beyond the pass/fail status, agent developers need to understand whether a particular interaction style leads to wasteful changes or regressions, such as unnecessary large-scale rewrites. We therefore formalize waste as modifications to files that were not modified in the corresponding golden run and additional tokens spent compared with the golden run. We define regression as tests that fail after the agent’s changes but were previously passing. Based on these definitions, we hypothesize that different user personas will lead to varying levels of waste and regression compared with the baseline SWE-Bench issue.
paragraphs.zh: 除了通过/失败状态之外，智能体开发者还需要了解某种特定的交互风格是否会导致浪费性的修改或回归，例如不必要的大规模重写。 因此，我们将浪费形式化定义为：对在对应黄金运行中未被修改的文件所做的修改，以及与黄金运行相比额外消耗的令牌数。 我们将回归定义为：在智能体做出修改后失败的、但之前原本通过的测试。 基于这些定义，我们假设不同的用户画像将导致与基线 SWE-Bench 议题相比不同程度的浪费和回归。

paragraphs.en: Additionally, we are interested in comparing the performance of SWE-DIVE against the original benchmark results. Decomposing a task into smaller subtasks through multi-turn interactions could potentially improve the agent’s performance and make the benchmark less challenging. This is one of the reasons why we chose to evaluate smaller models rather than state-of-the-art, top-tier models, which already perform very well on the original benchmarks. This allows us to better investigate whether the interactive setting itself provides a performance advantage and how different models respond to the additional complexity introduced by multi-turn interactions.
paragraphs.zh: 此外，我们有兴趣将 SWE-DIVE 的性能与原始基准测试结果进行比较。 通过多轮交互将任务分解为更小的子任务，有可能提升智能体的性能，并使基准测试的挑战性降低。 这是我们选择评估较小的模型而非最先进顶级模型的原因之一，后者在原始基准测试中已经表现非常好。 这使我们能够更好地研究交互式设置本身是否能带来性能优势，以及不同模型如何应对多轮交互所带来的额外复杂性。

paragraphs.en: To demonstrate SWE-DIVE in practice, we conduct a qualitative evaluation of agent traces using an SWE-bench Verified ( Jimenez et al.,, 2024 ) task (astropy-12907); Figure 2 illustrates the results. The task addresses a bug in the separability_matrix function, which does not correctly compute separability for nested CompoundModels. We run SWE-DIVE with the OpenCode, (2026) agent using gemini-2.5-flash ( Google, 2025a, ) as the underlying model. We evaluate the agent using three personas—Expert Nitpicker, Vague Requester, and Mind Changer—resulting in three user-agent conversations (cf. Figures 3 – 5 ). We compared with the baseline agent without SWE-DIVE, where the agent resolved the task with a one-file, one-line patch, matching the golden solution.
paragraphs.zh: 为了在实践中展示 SWE-DIVE，我们使用 SWE-bench Verified（Jimenez et al.,, 2024）的一个任务（astropy-12907）对智能体轨迹进行了定性评估；图 2 展示了结果。 该任务针对 separability_matrix 函数中的一个 bug，该函数无法正确计算嵌套 CompoundModels 的可分离性。 我们使用 OpenCode（2026）智能体并以 gemini-2.5-flash（Google, 2025a,）作为底层模型来运行 SWE-DIVE。 我们使用三种人设来评估该智能体——Expert Nitpicker（专业挑剔者）、Vague Requester（模糊请求者）和 Mind Changer（改变主意者），从而产生了三段用户与智能体的对话（参见图 3–5）。 我们与不使用 SWE-DIVE 的基线智能体进行了对比，该智能体通过一个单文件、单行的补丁解决了任务，与黄金解答相吻合。

The agent successfully resolved the issue with both the Expert Nitpicker and Mind Changer personas, whereas the Vague Requester persona led the agent to fix the intended issue but also introduce additional changes that caused 10 previously passing tests to fail.

paragraphs.en: With the Expert Nitpicker, the agent resolved the issue within four turns. However, the user simulator identified two genuine problems in the agent’s implementation: code had been added to the wrong file, and an unrelated leftover change remained in the code. The user simulator provided small, scoped corrections to the existing implementation and then stopped, resulting in a successful resolution. However, the open-ended nature of the requests led the agent to perform a substantial rewrite. Finally, the Mind Changer persona also led the agent to successfully resolve the issue. paragraphs.en: Our preliminary results demonstrate how the SWE-DIVE benchmark can be used in practice. paragraphs.en: This user simulation enables a diverse range of use cases due to the variety of benchmarks implemented in the Harbor framework ( Harbor Framework Team,, 2026 ) . Additionally, it supports diverse user roles adapted from real-world users and inspired by SWE-Chat ( Baumann et al.,, 2026 ) . We define three user roles–Expert Nitpicker, Mind Changer, and Vague Requester–which differ in how users communicate requirements, provide feedback, and evolve their goals throughout the interaction. These roles provide controlled behavioral variation grounded in observed real-user interactions. While this diversity determines the range of user behaviors represented in the benchmark, the fidelity of the simulation depends on how closely these behaviors reflect real user interactions.
paragraphs.zh: 得益于 Harbor 框架（Harbor Framework Team,, 2026）中实现的多种基准测试，这种用户模拟能够支持多样化的用例。 此外，它还支持改编自真实用户并受 SWE-Chat（Baumann et al.,, 2026）启发的多种用户角色。 我们定义了三种用户角色——挑剔专家（Expert Nitpicker）、意见改变者（Mind Changer）和模糊请求者（Vague Requester）——它们在用户如何传达需求、提供反馈以及在交互过程中如何演变目标方面各不相同。 这些角色基于观察到的真实用户交互，提供了受控的行为变化。 虽然这种多样性决定了基准测试中所呈现的用户行为的范围，但模拟的真实性取决于这些行为在多大程度上贴近真实用户的交互。

paragraphs.en: SWE-DIVE aims to improve fidelity by modeling users as interactive participants rather than static prompt generators. The user simulator conditions each turn on the agent’s latest response and code changes, allowing simulated users to provide corrections, introduce follow-up requirements, or modify their requests as the interaction unfolds. These interactions are grounded in validated benchmark tasks and underlying user behaviors, enabling the user simulator to operate in a multi-turn environment while adopting one of the defined user roles. A direct comparison between SWE-DIVE trajectories and held-out human SWE-Chat trajectories remains an important direction for future work.
paragraphs.zh: SWE-DIVE 旨在通过将用户建模为交互式参与者而非静态提示生成器来提升保真度。 用户模拟器以智能体最新的回复和代码变更为条件生成每一轮对话，使模拟用户能够在交互过程中提供纠正、提出后续需求或修改其请求。 这些交互以经过验证的基准任务和底层用户行为为基础，使用户模拟器能够在多轮环境中运行，同时扮演所定义的用户角色之一。 将 SWE-DIVE 轨迹与留出的真实人类 SWE-Chat 轨迹进行直接比较仍是未来工作的重要方向。

paragraphs.en: Beyond fidelity, the interaction between the simulated user and the agent also raises an important question of validity: whether the use of different simulated users can affect the conclusions drawn from an evaluation. The qualitative trajectories provide an initial indication that this may be the case. On the same Astropy task, different simulated user behaviors resulted in distinct agent trajectories and outcomes: the Vague Requester induced broader changes that introduced regressions, whereas the Expert Nitpicker guided the agent toward a successful resolution through targeted corrections. These results suggest that the simulated user’s behavior can influence the observed performance of an agent and, consequently, the conclusions drawn from the evaluation.
